title: Online Orders Held at the Same Time
content:
A customer may hold any number of Online Orders orders at once. There is no cap on open orders per customer.

Each order stands on its own: it is priced, shipped, adjusted and refunded on its own, and thresholds such as free shipping are never met by combining two orders.

## The rule restated

| Question the rule answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| How many open Online Orders orders may one customer hold? | Any number; no cap applies |
| Is pricing worked out across a customer's orders together? | No; each order is priced on its own |
| Are shipping, adjustments and refunds handled per order? | Yes; each order is shipped, adjusted and refunded on its own |
| Can two orders be combined to reach a threshold such as free shipping? | Never |

## Illustration (hypothetical amounts)

A customer places two Online Orders orders on the same day, one with merchandise worth 70.00 after discounts and one worth 65.00. Each order is measured against the free-shipping threshold by itself, with 70.00 and 65.00 respectively; the combined 135.00 is never the figure tested.
